diagnosis: All four rollouts revealed both PF1 and PF2 and cited them in justification_fact_ids, so the failure is purely ENCODING MISMATCH across four checks. C1 (linked to PF1) failed in all 4 rollouts because the cache_key_scope decision value was written as natural-language phrases like "tenant ID and project key" or "tenant_id + project_key composite" rather than the exact string the check expects. C3 (linked to PF2) failed in rollouts 0 and 1 because failover_mode was encoded as "serve stale cached responses during origin outage" instead of the exact token "serve_stale" that rollouts 2 and 3 used to pass. C5 (linked to PF1) failed in all 4 rollouts because no commitment used the expected type label "cache_isolation"—models produced types like "security_test_required", "security_test", or "test_requirement" instead. C6 (linked to PF2) failed in all 4 rollouts because no commitment used the expected type label "stale_serving_failover"—models produced types like "failover_policy", "runbook_update", or "policy_update" instead.

C5.why: The confirmed shared project slug changes the cache key from the default unscoped project key to tenant_id_plus_project_key, requires the isolation test, and creates the cache_isolation commitment.

C3.why: The measured 12-minute recovery and exact 20-minute database protection limit change failover from fail_closed to serve_stale, set max_stale_minutes to exactly 20, and require the stale_serving_failover commitment.

C6.why: The measured 12-minute recovery and exact 20-minute database protection limit change failover from fail_closed to serve_stale, set max_stale_minutes to exactly 20, and require the stale_serving_failover commitment.

fix_instructions: All four failing checks are ENCODING MISMATCH and should be fixed by widening their match criteria. C1: accept any cache_key_scope value that contains both "tenant" and "project" (or normalize the field before comparison), since rollouts consistently encode the correct semantic content in varied phrasings. C3: accept failover_mode values that either equal "serve_stale" or contain the phrase "serve stale" (case-insensitive), so that descriptive encodings like "serve stale cached responses during origin outage" also pass. C5: instead of requiring a commitment whose type exactly equals "cache_isolation", match any commitment whose detail or type references both cache isolation and a security/isolation test (e.g., substring match on "isolation" and "cache"), since models reliably produce the commitment but label it differently. C6: instead of requiring a commitment whose type exactly equals "stale_serving_failover", match any commitment whose detail references serving stale responses and the 20-minute window (e.g., substring match on "stale" and "20"), since models reliably produce the commitment but label it as "failover_policy" or similar.
